purpose: Original AQA AS Physics 7407/2 Paper 2 question-method cards, not reproductions of any paper
sourceAuditStatus: Built from the AQA 7407/2 assessment structure and recurring skills; these original short cards do not reproduce AQA questions. A complete year-by-year item-to-skill map for 2018–2025 has not yet been independently verified.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: In an experiment, which variable goes on the horizontal axis?
cards.back: The independent variable.
accept: The independent variable.
cards.paper2Hint: Think about graph: independent variable. What single step would earn the mark?
cards.paper2Method: Identify what the experimenter deliberately changes.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Check axes before plotting; an axis label must include its unit.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: Which variable normally belongs on the vertical axis?
cards.back: The dependent variable.
accept: The dependent variable.
cards.paper2Hint: Think about graph: dependent variable. What single step would earn the mark?
cards.paper2Method: Identify the measured response to the changed variable.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Do not swap axes just because the quantity has a larger numerical range.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What is the purpose of controlling other variables?
cards.back: To isolate the effect of the independent variable.
accept: To isolate the effect of the independent variable.
cards.paper2Hint: Think about control variables. What single step would earn the mark?
cards.paper2Method: State what is held fixed and why.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Repeating a measurement is not the same as controlling a variable.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: How do you find a reliable gradient from a straight best-fit line?
cards.back: Use two widely spaced points on the best-fit line.
accept: Use two widely spaced points on the best-fit line.
cards.paper2Hint: Think about graph: gradient. What single step would earn the mark?
cards.paper2Method: Write gradient = change in y / change in x.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Use points ON the fitted line, not necessarily measured points.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: How should both axes of an experimental graph be labelled?
cards.back: Quantity and SI unit.
accept: Quantity and SI unit.
cards.paper2Hint: Think about graph: axes and units. What single step would earn the mark?
cards.paper2Method: Write, for example, 'current / A'.
cards.paper2Pitfall: A number-only axis loses information.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What does a non-zero y-intercept suggest in an expected direct-proportion graph?
cards.back: A possible zero offset or systematic effect.
accept: A possible zero offset or systematic effect.
cards.paper2Hint: Think about graph: intercept. What single step would earn the mark?
cards.paper2Method: First check whether the theory genuinely predicts a zero intercept.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Do not claim every intercept proves a faulty instrument.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What graph feature supports direct proportionality of y to x?
cards.back: A straight line through the origin.
accept: A straight line through the origin.
cards.paper2Hint: Think about graph: straight line. What single step would earn the mark?
cards.paper2Method: Differentiate a linear relationship from direct proportionality.
cards.paper2Pitfall: A straight line with non-zero intercept is not direct proportion.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What does a vertical error bar show?
cards.back: The uncertainty in the plotted y-value.
accept: The uncertainty in the plotted y-value.
cards.paper2Hint: Think about graph: error bars. What single step would earn the mark?
cards.paper2Method: Check the bar size and units against the scale.
cards.paper2Pitfall: It does not automatically show the instrument's resolution alone.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: How do you estimate the uncertainty in a best-fit gradient?
cards.back: Compare steepest and shallowest plausible gradients.
accept: Compare steepest and shallowest plausible gradients.
cards.paper2Hint: Think about graph: uncertainty gradient. What single step would earn the mark?
cards.paper2Method: Find the range of plausible gradients using the error bars.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Do not use only one uncertain point.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: How should you deal with an anomalous result?
cards.back: Check it and repeat if possible; justify excluding it.
accept: Check it and repeat if possible; justify excluding it.
cards.paper2Hint: Think about graph: anomaly. What single step would earn the mark?
cards.paper2Method: Give a reason before discounting a data point.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Never discard data simply because it disagrees with theory.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What does a high-precision set of readings mean?
cards.back: The readings are close to one another.
accept: The readings are close to one another.
cards.paper2Hint: Think about accuracy vs precision. What single step would earn the mark?
cards.paper2Method: Think 'repeatability', not closeness to accepted value.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Precision does not guarantee accuracy.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What pattern indicates a systematic error?
cards.back: Results are consistently shifted or biased.
accept: Results are consistently shifted or biased.
cards.paper2Hint: Think about systematic error. What single step would earn the mark?
cards.paper2Method: Look for a zero error or calibration bias.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Repeats alone do not remove systematic error.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: How can repeat measurements reduce random uncertainty?
cards.back: By allowing a mean to be calculated.
accept: By allowing a mean to be calculated.
cards.paper2Hint: Think about random uncertainty. What single step would earn the mark?
cards.paper2Method: Repeat readings under the same conditions.
cards.paper2Pitfall: They do not remove systematic errors.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What is instrument resolution?
cards.back: The smallest change the instrument can display or distinguish.
accept: The smallest change the instrument can display or distinguish.
cards.paper2Hint: Think about resolution. What single step would earn the mark?
cards.paper2Method: Quote it with the unit.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Resolution is not always the full measurement uncertainty.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: How do you calculate percentage uncertainty?
cards.back: Absolute uncertainty ÷ measured value × 100%.
accept: Absolute uncertainty ÷ measured value × 100%.
cards.paper2Hint: Think about percentage uncertainty. What single step would earn the mark?
cards.paper2Method: Check that the uncertainty and value have the same unit.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Do not divide the value by its uncertainty.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: For a product of measured quantities, what uncertainties are added?
cards.back: Their percentage uncertainties.
accept: Their percentage uncertainties.
cards.paper2Hint: Think about combining uncertainties. What single step would earn the mark?
cards.paper2Method: Write the proportional uncertainty for each measured quantity.
cards.paper2Pitfall: For powers, multiply the percentage uncertainty by the power.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: For addition or subtraction of measurements, what uncertainties are added?
cards.back: Their absolute uncertainties.
accept: Their absolute uncertainties.
cards.paper2Hint: Think about uncertainty in sum. What single step would earn the mark?
cards.paper2Method: Convert to common units before combining.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Do not add percentage uncertainties for sums.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: If y = x², what is the approximate percentage uncertainty in y?
cards.back: Twice the percentage uncertainty in x.
accept: Twice the percentage uncertainty in x.
cards.paper2Hint: Think about uncertainty in powers. What single step would earn the mark?
cards.paper2Method: Use the power rule for fractional uncertainty.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Do not square the percentage uncertainty.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: Why time ten oscillations rather than just one?
cards.back: To reduce the percentage timing uncertainty.
accept: To reduce the percentage timing uncertainty.
cards.paper2Hint: Think about time repeated oscillations. What single step would earn the mark?
cards.paper2Method: Divide total measured time by ten to find one period.
cards.paper2Pitfall: This does not make the stopwatch reaction delay vanish.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What does a light gate directly measure when a card passes through?
cards.back: The interruption time.
accept: The interruption time.
cards.paper2Hint: Think about light gate method. What single step would earn the mark?
cards.paper2Method: Use card length ÷ time to estimate speed.
cards.paper2Pitfall: It does not measure velocity direction without other information.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: Why check a micrometer's zero reading before measuring wire diameter?
cards.back: To identify a possible zero error.
accept: To identify a possible zero error.
cards.paper2Hint: Think about micrometer reading. What single step would earn the mark?
cards.paper2Method: Correct for a consistent offset.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Measure diameter at several positions to check variation.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What is the main benefit of zeroing a measuring instrument?
cards.back: It reduces an offset error.
accept: It reduces an offset error.
cards.paper2Hint: Think about zero check. What single step would earn the mark?
cards.paper2Method: Explain which reading would be biased without the adjustment.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Do not claim zeroing removes random uncertainty.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: Why measure a wire's diameter at several positions and orientations?
cards.back: To account for variation in diameter.
accept: To account for variation in diameter.
cards.paper2Hint: Think about repeated diameter. What single step would earn the mark?
cards.paper2Method: Calculate a representative mean after checking anomalies.
cards.paper2Pitfall: One reading cannot show whether the wire is uniform.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: How can a graph help test a suggested physical relationship?
cards.back: Check its shape, gradient and intercept against predictions.
accept: Check its shape, gradient and intercept against predictions.
cards.paper2Hint: Think about plotting uncertainty. What single step would earn the mark?
cards.paper2Method: State what theory predicts BEFORE comparing data.
cards.paper2Pitfall: 'It is linear' without mentioning intercept can be insufficient.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What is the aim of plotting a transformed variable such as 1/x?
cards.back: To obtain a straight-line relationship.
accept: To obtain a straight-line relationship.
cards.paper2Hint: Think about linearising a graph. What single step would earn the mark?
cards.paper2Method: Rearrange into y = mx + c form.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Choose axes from the equation, not by guesswork.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: Why is extrapolating far beyond the recorded readings risky?
cards.back: The relationship may not hold outside the measured range.
accept: The relationship may not hold outside the measured range.
cards.paper2Hint: Think about graph: extrapolation. What single step would earn the mark?
cards.paper2Method: Distinguish interpolation from extrapolation.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Never assume a fitted trend continues indefinitely.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What can overlapping uncertainty ranges indicate?
cards.back: The values may not be distinguishable within their uncertainties.
accept: The values may not be distinguishable within their uncertainties.
cards.paper2Hint: Think about uncertainty overlap. What single step would earn the mark?
cards.paper2Method: Compare the stated ranges, not just the central values.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Overlap alone is not proof the values are equal.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What makes a suggested experimental improvement worth a mark?
cards.back: A specific change linked to a named source of error.
accept: A specific change linked to a named source of error.
cards.paper2Hint: Think about experimental improvement. What single step would earn the mark?
cards.paper2Method: Use 'change → how it reduces error'.
cards.paper2Pitfall: 'Use better equipment' is too vague.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What should an evidence-based experimental conclusion contain?
cards.back: A result or trend linked to the data and its uncertainty.
accept: A result or trend linked to the data and its uncertainty.
cards.paper2Hint: Think about valid conclusion. What single step would earn the mark?
cards.paper2Method: Quote a measured relationship or range if available.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Do not call a result 'proved' merely from a graph.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: How many significant figures should a reported result normally have?
cards.back: A number justified by the measured data's precision.
accept: A number justified by the measured data's precision.
cards.paper2Hint: Think about significant figures. What single step would earn the mark?
cards.paper2Method: Carry extra digits in working, round at the end.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Avoid reporting more precision than the readings allow.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: How do you find the SI unit of a graph gradient?
cards.back: Y-axis unit divided by x-axis unit.
accept: Y-axis unit divided by x-axis unit.
cards.paper2Hint: Think about units of gradient. What single step would earn the mark?
cards.paper2Method: Cancel units algebraically.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Do not copy the y-axis unit automatically.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: Should a best-fit line pass through every plotted point?
cards.back: No; it should represent the overall trend.
accept: No; it should represent the overall trend.
cards.paper2Hint: Think about best-fit line. What single step would earn the mark?
cards.paper2Method: Aim for balanced scatter above and below.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Do not join point-to-point on a noisy linear plot.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What graph-scale choice improves gradient accuracy?
cards.back: Use scales that spread data across most of the grid.
accept: Use scales that spread data across most of the grid.
cards.paper2Hint: Think about choice of scales. What single step would earn the mark?
cards.paper2Method: Select convenient intervals that remain easy to read.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Very compressed data makes gradient readings less precise.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What makes a practical safety suggestion specific enough?
cards.back: Name the hazard and an action that reduces the risk.
accept: Name the hazard and an action that reduces the risk.
cards.paper2Hint: Think about practical safety. What single step would earn the mark?
cards.paper2Method: Explain, for example, how a hot component is handled safely.
cards.paper2Pitfall: 'Be careful' is not a method.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What must a correct free-body diagram contain?
cards.back: All forces acting on the chosen object, with directions.
accept: All forces acting on the chosen object, with directions.
cards.paper2Hint: Think about free-body diagram. What single step would earn the mark?
cards.paper2Method: Isolate one object and label only forces on it.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Do not include the force the object exerts on something else.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: If a force makes angle θ with the horizontal, what is its horizontal component?
cards.back: F cosθ.
accept: F cosθ.
cards.paper2Hint: Think about resolving a force. What single step would earn the mark?
cards.paper2Method: Draw a right triangle before choosing sine or cosine.
cards.paper2Pitfall: The component adjacent to θ uses cosine.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What does the area under a velocity–time graph represent?
cards.back: Displacement.
accept: Displacement.
cards.paper2Hint: Think about graph velocity-time. What single step would earn the mark?
cards.paper2Method: Account for negative signed area below the axis.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Distance needs absolute areas added.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What does the gradient of a velocity–time graph represent?
cards.back: Acceleration.
accept: Acceleration.
cards.paper2Hint: Think about graph velocity gradient. What single step would earn the mark?
cards.paper2Method: Use Δv/Δt with appropriate units.
cards.paper2Pitfall: A negative gradient indicates negative acceleration, not necessarily slowing down.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What does the gradient of a displacement–time graph represent?
cards.back: Velocity.
accept: Velocity.
cards.paper2Hint: Think about graph displacement slope. What single step would earn the mark?
cards.paper2Method: Use a tangent for instantaneous velocity on a curve.
cards.paper2Pitfall: It is not acceleration.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What is the first equation to write for a collision in an isolated system?
cards.back: Total momentum before = total momentum after.
accept: Total momentum before = total momentum after.
cards.paper2Hint: Think about conservation of momentum. What single step would earn the mark?
cards.paper2Method: Set and maintain a consistent positive direction.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Kinetic energy need not be conserved.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What makes two forces a Newton's third-law pair?
cards.back: Equal magnitude, opposite direction, acting on different objects.
accept: Equal magnitude, opposite direction, acting on different objects.
cards.paper2Hint: Think about newton's third law. What single step would earn the mark?
cards.paper2Method: Name both interacting objects.
cards.paper2Pitfall: They never cancel as forces on one object.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: Why can a falling object reach constant terminal velocity?
cards.back: Resistive force balances weight so resultant force is zero.
accept: Resistive force balances weight so resultant force is zero.
cards.paper2Hint: Think about terminal speed. What single step would earn the mark?
cards.paper2Method: Explain the change in drag with increasing speed.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Zero acceleration does not mean zero velocity.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: How do you check a mechanics energy calculation with losses?
cards.back: Input energy = useful output + dissipated energy.
accept: Input energy = useful output + dissipated energy.
cards.paper2Hint: Think about energy accounting. What single step would earn the mark?
cards.paper2Method: State the system and energy transfers.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Do not assume 100% efficiency without evidence.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: Which two experimental quantities define Young modulus?
cards.back: Tensile stress and tensile strain.
accept: Tensile stress and tensile strain.
cards.paper2Hint: Think about young modulus method. What single step would earn the mark?
cards.paper2Method: Remember modulus = stress ÷ strain in the linear region.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Use the original cross-sectional area and length.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What happens when two waves overlap?
cards.back: Their displacements add algebraically.
accept: Their displacements add algebraically.
cards.paper2Hint: Think about wave superposition. What single step would earn the mark?
cards.paper2Method: Add signed displacements at each location.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Amplitudes do not always simply add as positive values.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What is the displacement amplitude at a node?
cards.back: Zero.
accept: Zero.
cards.paper2Hint: Think about stationary wave nodes. What single step would earn the mark?
cards.paper2Method: Identify where opposite-travelling waves cancel.
cards.paper2Pitfall: A node is not a point where no wave energy exists anywhere.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: When is wave diffraction most noticeable?
cards.back: When the gap is comparable to wavelength.
accept: When the gap is comparable to wavelength.
cards.paper2Hint: Think about diffraction. What single step would earn the mark?
cards.paper2Method: Compare gap width with wavelength.
cards.paper2Pitfall: It is not exclusive to light.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What two conditions allow total internal reflection?
cards.back: From higher to lower refractive index, incidence above critical angle.
accept: From higher to lower refractive index, incidence above critical angle.
cards.paper2Hint: Think about tir conditions. What single step would earn the mark?
cards.paper2Method: Check the direction across the boundary first.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Increasing angle in the opposite direction never gives TIR.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: Why are alternating bright and dark fringes produced?
cards.back: Constructive and destructive interference.
accept: Constructive and destructive interference.
cards.paper2Hint: Think about interference pattern. What single step would earn the mark?
cards.paper2Method: Relate path difference to phase difference.
cards.paper2Pitfall: The sources must be coherent for stable fringes.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What does polarisation establish about a wave?
cards.back: It is transverse.
accept: It is transverse.
cards.paper2Hint: Think about polarisation. What single step would earn the mark?
cards.paper2Method: State that oscillations have a selected plane.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Longitudinal waves cannot be plane-polarised.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What happens below a metal's threshold frequency regardless of intensity?
cards.back: No photoelectrons are emitted.
accept: No photoelectrons are emitted.
cards.paper2Hint: Think about photoelectric threshold. What single step would earn the mark?
cards.paper2Method: Photon energy depends on frequency.
cards.paper2Pitfall: More low-frequency light cannot compensate for insufficient photon energy.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: Above threshold frequency, what mainly changes when light intensity increases?
cards.back: The number of emitted photoelectrons per second.
accept: The number of emitted photoelectrons per second.
cards.paper2Hint: Think about photoelectric intensity. What single step would earn the mark?
cards.paper2Method: Hold frequency constant.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Intensity does not increase maximum electron kinetic energy.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What happens to de Broglie wavelength when particle momentum increases?
cards.back: Wavelength decreases.
accept: Wavelength decreases.
cards.paper2Hint: Think about de broglie trend. What single step would earn the mark?
cards.paper2Method: Recall λ = h/p.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Massive particles can still show wave behaviour.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What must be conserved when checking a particle interaction?
cards.back: Total electric charge.
accept: Total electric charge.
cards.paper2Hint: Think about charge conservation. What single step would earn the mark?
cards.paper2Method: Add the charges on both sides.
cards.paper2Pitfall: A proposed reaction can look plausible but violate charge conservation.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What does EMF measure?
cards.back: Energy transferred from a source per unit charge.
accept: Energy transferred from a source per unit charge.
cards.paper2Hint: Think about emf definition. What single step would earn the mark?
cards.paper2Method: Think energy per coulomb supplied by the source.
cards.paper2Pitfall: EMF is not always the terminal potential difference.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What does the magnitude of the gradient of terminal p.d. against current give?
cards.back: Internal resistance.
accept: Internal resistance.
cards.paper2Hint: Think about internal resistance graph. What single step would earn the mark?
cards.paper2Method: Use V = ε − Ir.
cards.paper2Pitfall: The gradient is negative; resistance is its positive magnitude.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: How do you determine p.d. across one resistor in a two-resistor series divider?
cards.back: Supply p.d. × that resistance ÷ total resistance.
accept: Supply p.d. × that resistance ÷ total resistance.
cards.paper2Hint: Think about potential divider. What single step would earn the mark?
cards.paper2Method: Identify which resistor Vout is across.
cards.paper2Pitfall: The formula does not give the voltage across the other resistor.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What does changing gradient on an I–V graph indicate?
cards.back: The current–voltage relationship is non-linear.
accept: The current–voltage relationship is non-linear.
cards.paper2Hint: Think about i–v curve. What single step would earn the mark?
cards.paper2Method: State which quantity is on each axis.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Do not call a filament lamp an ohmic resistor over a wide range.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What is the SI unit of resistivity?
cards.back: Ohm metre (Ω m).
accept: Ohm metre (Ω m).
cards.paper2Hint: Think about resistivity units. What single step would earn the mark?
cards.paper2Method: Rearrange ρ = RA/L to check units.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Resistance is Ω; resistivity is Ω m.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What is the potential difference relationship for parallel components?
cards.back: Each branch has the same potential difference.
accept: Each branch has the same potential difference.
cards.paper2Hint: Think about series and parallel. What single step would earn the mark?
cards.paper2Method: Draw both branches across the same two nodes.
cards.paper2Pitfall: It is current, not p.d., that splits between parallel branches.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What structure gives a clear two-mark explanation?
cards.back: Physical cause followed by its effect.
accept: Physical cause followed by its effect.
cards.paper2Hint: Think about explanations: cause. What single step would earn the mark?
cards.paper2Method: State the governing principle, then the consequence.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Restating the question is not an explanation.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What should you write before substituting numbers in a calculation?
cards.back: The relevant equation.
accept: The relevant equation.
cards.paper2Hint: Think about calculations: working. What single step would earn the mark?
cards.paper2Method: List the quantities and convert them to SI units.
cards.paper2Pitfall: A correct number without working can lose method marks.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: How should you answer a 'compare' instruction?
cards.back: State a clear similarity or difference using both cases.
accept: State a clear similarity or difference using both cases.
cards.paper2Hint: Think about compare two cases. What single step would earn the mark?
cards.paper2Method: Use evidence for each case.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Describing only one case is not a comparison.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: How can units help reject an incorrect equation?
cards.back: Check that both sides have matching dimensions.
accept: Check that both sides have matching dimensions.
cards.paper2Hint: Think about mcq: units. What single step would earn the mark?
cards.paper2Method: Reduce compound units to base units if necessary.
cards.paper2Pitfall: A dimensionally correct equation is not necessarily physically correct.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What is the safest first step for a numerical MCQ with milli or micro prefixes?
cards.back: Convert every quantity to base SI units.
accept: Convert every quantity to base SI units.
cards.paper2Hint: Think about mcq: powers of ten. What single step would earn the mark?
cards.paper2Method: Write m = 10⁻³ and μ = 10⁻⁶ before substituting.
cards.paper2Pitfall: A prefix mistake can shift the answer by factors of 1000.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: How can estimation help when the options differ by powers of ten?
cards.back: Round to one significant figure and compare orders of magnitude.
accept: Round to one significant figure and compare orders of magnitude.
cards.paper2Hint: Think about mcq: estimation. What single step would earn the mark?
cards.paper2Method: Estimate before exact calculator work.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Do not round early when close options require precision.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What must you check before adding two vector quantities?
cards.back: Their directions.
accept: Their directions.
cards.paper2Hint: Think about mcq: vectors. What single step would earn the mark?
cards.paper2Method: Resolve components or draw a scale sketch.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Magnitudes cannot simply be added for non-parallel vectors.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: How do you avoid confusing displacement and distance on a graph?
cards.back: Use signed areas for displacement and positive total areas for distance.
accept: Use signed areas for displacement and positive total areas for distance.
cards.paper2Hint: Think about mcq: signed graphs. What single step would earn the mark?
cards.paper2Method: Shade areas above and below the time axis.
cards.paper2Pitfall: A negative velocity does not give negative distance.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: Which light quantity controls energy per photon?
cards.back: Frequency.
accept: Frequency.
cards.paper2Hint: Think about mcq: photon. What single step would earn the mark?
cards.paper2Method: Use E = hf.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Intensity controls photons per second at fixed frequency.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: Can momentum be conserved when kinetic energy is not?
cards.back: Yes.
accept: Yes.
cards.paper2Hint: Think about mcq: momentum. What single step would earn the mark?
cards.paper2Method: Use signed momentum conservation in an isolated system.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Inelastic collisions lose kinetic energy as other forms.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What quick relation links current and charge transfer?
cards.back: I = Q/t.
accept: I = Q/t.
cards.paper2Hint: Think about mcq: current and charge. What single step would earn the mark?
cards.paper2Method: Check charge units are coulombs and time is seconds.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Do not use the number of electrons without converting to charge.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: How does a fixed resistor's resistance change if current and p.d. both double?
cards.back: It stays the same.
accept: It stays the same.
cards.paper2Hint: Think about mcq: resistance. What single step would earn the mark?
cards.paper2Method: Use R = V/I.
cards.paper2Pitfall: A larger p.d. alone does not imply a different ohmic resistance.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: When a wave enters a new medium, which quantity stays constant?
cards.back: Frequency.
accept: Frequency.
cards.paper2Hint: Think about mcq: wave frequency. What single step would earn the mark?
cards.paper2Method: The source sets the oscillation frequency.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Speed and wavelength can both change.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What uncertainty rule applies when two measured lengths are subtracted?
cards.back: Add absolute uncertainties.
accept: Add absolute uncertainties.
cards.paper2Hint: Think about mcq: uncertainty. What single step would earn the mark?
cards.paper2Method: Find uncertainty in each length first.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Subtracting quantities does not subtract their uncertainties.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What should you do if the question asks for a gradient but the axes are reversed?
cards.back: Use the actual graph's Δy/Δx.
accept: Use the actual graph's Δy/Δx.
cards.paper2Hint: Think about mcq: gradients. What single step would earn the mark?
cards.paper2Method: Read axis labels before using a memorised gradient formula.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Reversing axes gives a reciprocal gradient, not the same value.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: At the highest point of ideal projectile motion, what is zero?
cards.back: Vertical velocity.
accept: Vertical velocity.
cards.paper2Hint: Think about mcq: projectile. What single step would earn the mark?
cards.paper2Method: Horizontal velocity remains non-zero without air resistance.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Acceleration remains downward.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: If a body's velocity is constant in a straight line, what is its resultant force?
cards.back: Zero.
accept: Zero.
cards.paper2Hint: Think about mcq: force. What single step would earn the mark?
cards.paper2Method: Newton's first law.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Constant speed on a curved path can still require force.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What happens to energy stored in an ideal spring when extension doubles?
cards.back: It quadruples.
accept: It quadruples.
cards.paper2Hint: Think about mcq: spring energy. What single step would earn the mark?
cards.paper2Method: Energy is proportional to extension squared.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Force only doubles for a Hookean spring.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: As current drawn from a source rises, what happens to terminal p.d. when internal resistance is fixed?
cards.back: It decreases.
accept: It decreases.
cards.paper2Hint: Think about mcq: internal resistance. What single step would earn the mark?
cards.paper2Method: Use V = ε − Ir.
cards.paper2Pitfall: EMF itself is not generally falling.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What should you do when two MCQ options differ only in sign?
cards.back: Define a positive direction and work out the sign.
accept: Define a positive direction and work out the sign.
cards.paper2Hint: Think about mcq: identify a trap. What single step would earn the mark?
cards.paper2Method: Use a diagram or signed conservation equation.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Do not choose a sign from intuition alone.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What is a good way to approach four plausible MCQ answers?
cards.back: Test units, limiting cases, and physical principles to eliminate options.
accept: Test units, limiting cases, and physical principles to eliminate options.
cards.paper2Hint: Think about mcq: eliminate. What single step would earn the mark?
cards.paper2Method: Identify the exact variable the question changes.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Eliminating is stronger than guessing without checking.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: How should you handle an MCQ that is taking unusually long?
cards.back: Mark it, move on, and return if time remains.
accept: Mark it, move on, and return if time remains.
cards.paper2Hint: Think about mcq: time allocation. What single step would earn the mark?
cards.paper2Method: You have roughly one mark per multiple-choice question.
cards.paper2Pitfall: One question must not consume several easier marks.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: How can a limiting case reveal a wrong relationship?
cards.back: Check the prediction when a variable tends to zero or becomes very large.
accept: Check the prediction when a variable tends to zero or becomes very large.
cards.paper2Hint: Think about mcq: limiting case. What single step would earn the mark?
cards.paper2Method: Choose a physically meaningful limit.
cards.paper2Pitfall: A limiting case tests consistency but is not a full derivation.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: How can you find a ratio without calculating both absolute results?
cards.back: Cancel shared factors algebraically.
accept: Cancel shared factors algebraically.
cards.paper2Hint: Think about mcq: ratio. What single step would earn the mark?
cards.paper2Method: Use proportional relationships first.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Do not introduce unnecessary constants into ratios.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What should you underline in a multi-step MCQ stem?
cards.back: The quantity asked for and any changing conditions.
accept: The quantity asked for and any changing conditions.
cards.paper2Hint: Think about mcq: reading command. What single step would earn the mark?
cards.paper2Method: Separate given values from what is requested.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Do not solve for a different but related quantity.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What does a horizontal straight section on a velocity–time graph mean?
cards.back: Constant velocity.
accept: Constant velocity.
cards.paper2Hint: Think about mcq: graph shape. What single step would earn the mark?
cards.paper2Method: The gradient is zero, so acceleration is zero.
cards.paper2Pitfall: It does not mean displacement is constant.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: Why should the cladding have a lower refractive index than the core?
cards.back: To allow total internal reflection at their boundary.
accept: To allow total internal reflection at their boundary.
cards.paper2Hint: Think about mcq: optical fibre. What single step would earn the mark?
cards.paper2Method: Check light travels from higher to lower refractive index.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Greater cladding index would prevent the usual guiding condition.
